Data: [gapminder](https://jennybc.github.io/gapminder/) by Jennifer Bryan (CC0),
read from the package's
[TSV file on GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jennybc/gapminder/refs/heads/main/inst/extdata/gapminder.tsv).
Based on free material from [GAPMINDER.ORG](https://www.gapminder.org/data/), CC-BY LICENSE.

```{python}
#| label: setup
#| warning: false
#| message: false

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jennybc/gapminder/refs/heads/main/inst/extdata/gapminder.tsv"
gapminder = pd.read_csv(url, sep="\t")
```

Setting up, loading required libraries. The dataset is loaded from GitHub through a URL. Internet connection is required for loading the data.

```{python}
#| label: explore-data
gapminder.info()

# Coverage: how many countries, which years, any missing values?
coverage = pd.DataFrame({
    "n_rows": [len(gapminder)],
    "n_countries": [gapminder["country"].nunique()],
    "first_year": [gapminder["year"].min()],
    "last_year": [gapminder["year"].max()],
    "missing_values": [gapminder.isna().sum().sum()],
})
display(coverage)

# Does every country have all survey years? (needed to compare 1952 with 2007)
(
    gapminder.groupby("country")["year"]
    .count()
    .value_counts()
    .rename_axis("years_per_country")
    .reset_index(name="n_countries")
)
```

First, we explore the data. The dataset has 1,704 rows and six columns: country, continent, year, life
expectancy, population, and GDP per capita. It covers 142 countries surveyed
every five years from 1952 to 2007, and there are no missing values. The last
table confirms that every country appears in all 12 survey years, so each
country has both a 1952 and a 2007 value to compare. GDP per capita is
measured in inflation-adjusted international dollars, which makes values
comparable across countries and years.

```{python}
#| label: wrangle-data
# One row per country, one column per year, values = GDP per capita
gdp_wide = gapminder.pivot(index="country", columns="year", values="gdpPercap")

# Growth from 1952 to 2007 for every country
growth = pd.DataFrame({
    "continent": gapminder.groupby("country")["continent"].first(),
    "gdp_1952": gdp_wide[1952],
    "gdp_2007": gdp_wide[2007],
})
growth["growth_pct"] = (growth["gdp_2007"] / growth["gdp_1952"] - 1) * 100

# Top 5 countries by percentage growth
top5 = growth.sort_values("growth_pct", ascending=False).head(5).round(1)
top5
```

The five countries with the highest growth are Equatorial Guinea, Taiwan,
South Korea, Singapore, and Botswana. Equatorial Guinea displays the largest growth by far: 
its GDP per capita in 2007 was about 32 times its 1952 level.
Taiwan and South Korea each grew roughly 23 to 24 times, Singapore about 20
times, and Botswana about 15 times. Three of the five are in East and
Southeast Asia and two are in Africa. Most of these countries started from a
low GDP per capita in 1952; Singapore started higher and still ranks fourth.

```{python}
#| label: fig-gdp-growth-python
#| fig-cap: "GDP per capita relative to 1952 for the five countries with the highest growth, 1952–2007. A value of 10 means ten times the 1952 level."
top5_data = gapminder[gapminder["country"].isin(top5.index)].copy()
top5_data["gdp_index"] = top5_data["gdpPercap"] / top5_data["country"].map(growth["gdp_1952"])

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
for country in top5.index:
    country_data = top5_data[top5_data["country"] == country]
    ax.plot(country_data["year"], country_data["gdp_index"], marker="o", label=country)
ax.axhline(1, color="grey", linestyle="--", linewidth=1)
ax.set_xlabel("Year")
ax.set_ylabel("GDP per capita relative to 1952 (1952 = 1)")
ax.legend(title="Country")
plt.show()
```

@fig-gdp-growth-python shows two different routes to the top five. Taiwan, South
Korea, and Singapore grew steadily from the 1960s onward, with growth
building on itself over four decades. Botswana followed a similar path
starting in the late 1960s. Equatorial Guinea looks very different: its GDP
per capita barely moved for forty years, and nearly all of its growth came
after 1992, when it rose from about three times its 1952 level to over
thirty times by 2007.

## Conclusion

Equatorial Guinea, Taiwan, South Korea, Singapore, and Botswana had the
highest growth in GDP per capita between 1952 and 2007.
